constraints: every row has the same length
clarifyingQuestions: Are regions connected horizontally and vertically only, or diagonally too?
Is a region score its size times its crowns, and does a region with no crowns score 0?
Can the board contain empty tiles or a castle tile?
hints: Group tiles into same-terrain regions with BFS or DFS.
While exploring one region, count its tiles and add up its crowns.
Use an explicit queue over row-major indices so a 1e5-tile region needs no recursion.
invariants: every tile belongs to exactly one region
the result is the sum over regions of size x crowns
chooseWhen: Grid connectivity with a per-component aggregate
tradeoffs: BFS and union-find are both linear here; BFS is simpler, union-find suits incremental boards
hack2hire:6a02333a2608e589a944a29d.variantLabel: Inferred single variant: sum of region size x region crowns

clarifyingQuestions: Should the answer list every process, or only a total or the maximum?
Is a process with no later smaller priority reported as 0?
Is the comparison strict (smaller, not smaller or equal)?
hints: Only the farthest smaller priority to the right matters.
The minimum of priorities[j..n-1] can only grow as j moves right.
Binary-search that suffix-minimum array for the last position whose minimum is still below priorities[i].
invariants: result[i] = 0 or result[i] = j - i with priorities[j] < priorities[i] and no larger index qualifies
suffixMin is non-decreasing
chooseWhen: Farthest (not nearest) smaller element to the right
tradeoffs: A monotonic stack finds nearest smaller elements, not the farthest; the suffix-minimum search is O(n log n) and simple
hack2hire:6a94a962cddc54478ddf6084.variantLabel: Inferred single variant: starvation time of every process

clarifyingQuestions: Should intervals with no prices produce a candlestick (for example carrying the previous close)?
Is the input sorted by time?
Can two pairs share a time?
In what order are the five fields returned?
hints: The interval of a time t starts at t - t mod 10.
Sorting by time makes the open the first pair and the close the last pair of each interval.
Sweep the sorted pairs, keep a running max and min, and emit a row when the interval start changes.
invariants: rows are strictly increasing by start
min <= open, close <= max in every row
chooseWhen: Bucketing a time series into fixed windows
tradeoffs: A hash map of buckets avoids sorting all pairs but then needs the bucket keys sorted and per-bucket earliest/latest tracking
hack2hire:67eb0d624c9bb801bfd0ef6b.variantLabel: Inferred single variant: 10-unit candlesticks over non-empty intervals

clarifyingQuestions: Is there a chunk size, and what happens to the last partial chunk?
Can inner lists be empty?
Should an empty stream return [] or [[]]?
hints: Ignore the inner-list boundaries: only the order of values matters.
Keep one buffer and push values until it holds size of them.
After the stream ends, emit the buffer if it is not empty.
invariants: every chunk except the last has exactly size values
concatenating the chunks gives the stream
chooseWhen: Batching a stream whose producer used different batch sizes
tradeoffs: Flattening first is simpler but holds an extra copy; streaming builds the chunks directly
hack2hire:69bf10b121f6ab4226963d68.variantLabel: Inferred single variant: fixed-size re-chunking of a stream of lists

clarifyingQuestions: Which rules follow the duplicate check, and what are their failure reasons?
Does a valid new association become visible to later ones in the same batch?
What string marks a valid association?
hints: Build constant-time lookups from the existing associations first.
A triple key answers rule 1; a (company, role) key answers rule 2.
Insert both keys when an association is accepted so later items in the batch see it.
invariants: a triple accepted once is reported ALREADY_EXISTS if repeated
at most one accepted new association per (company, role) not already present
chooseWhen: Batch validation against a growing set
tradeoffs: Two hash sets cost memory proportional to the input; a sorted structure would allow range queries that are not needed here
hack2hire:696294968742114304441df4.variantLabel: Inferred single variant: duplicate and role-conflict validation

constraints: rows are in preorder and every non-root value is the child of exactly one row
clarifyingQuestions: How is the tree passed in and returned?
Are promoted children inserted where the compressed node was, or appended?
What happens if compressedNodes contains the root or an unknown value?
hints: Promotion in place does not change the preorder of the nodes that stay.
A kept node's new parent is its nearest kept ancestor.
Process the preorder rows with an explicit stack so a 1e5-deep path needs no recursion.
invariants: the output preorder is the input preorder without compressed nodes
each kept node keeps its nearest kept ancestor as parent
chooseWhen: Removing internal nodes from a tree while keeping order
tradeoffs: Rebuilding from a flat preorder is linear but tied to that encoding; a pointer-based tree would splice child lists instead
hack2hire:67e4db7050b60b77022f386f.variantLabel: Inferred single variant: remove compressed nodes and promote their children

constraints: the sum over getMinSteps calls of the number of placed points is at most 2e6 (author testing bound)
clarifyingQuestions: What is the class called, and does adding an existing point do anything?
What do the queries return when a point was never added?
Does a move have to stop at the nearest point, or can it jump to any point on the line?
hints: Two points are connected exactly when their rows and columns are linked through other points: union-find over lines.
For distances, think of rows and columns as nodes: a point is an edge between its row and its column.
BFS from the start point's row and column; reaching a line at distance d lets every point on it be reached in d + 1 moves.
invariants: each row and column key is expanded at most once per BFS
two placed points are connected iff their rows share a union-find root
tradeoffs: BFS per query is linear in the component; precomputing all distances would cost quadratic memory
hack2hire:677595ec0d31dc201f712037.variantLabel: Inferred single variant: point connectivity and shortest move count

clarifyingQuestions: Is every sliding window counted, or do alerts reset after triggering?
Is the percentage test inclusive?
Is an hour bad when errors equal the threshold?
hints: Turn each hour into 0 or 1 (bad or not).
Slide a window of duration hours and keep its bad-hour count.
Compare bad * 100 with percent * duration to avoid fractions.
invariants: the window count equals the number of bad hours inside the current window
all comparisons are exact integers
tradeoffs: A prefix-sum array allows random window queries at the cost of O(n) memory
hack2hire:68001116c48db1937ce88f45.variantLabel: Inferred single variant: number of sliding windows that trigger

clarifyingQuestions: Are the counts returned in window order?
Can values be negative or repeated?
hints: Track how many times each value occurs in the window.
A value adds to the distinct count when its count goes from 0 to 1.
When the window slides, decrement the leaving value and drop it from the count when it reaches 0.
invariants: distinct equals the number of map keys with a positive count
the map holds only values of the current window
chooseWhen: Sliding windows over a stream of values
tradeoffs: A hash map is O(n) expected; sorting with coordinate compression gives a deterministic array-based variant
hack2hire:67e08fffa59c3d249d3625e0.variantLabel: Inferred single variant: distinct count per window

clarifyingQuestions: What are the three limits and their window lengths?
Do dropped requests count toward later windows?
Is the input sorted?
hints: Because the times are sorted, the k-th earlier request bounds a whole window.
Request i breaks the 20-per-10-seconds limit exactly when i >= 20 and requestTime[i] - requestTime[i - 20] < 10.
Check the three limits with i-3, i-20 and i-60 and count i once if any fails.
invariants: every request is counted at most once
dropped requests stay in the windows of later requests
tradeoffs: Index lookback needs sorted input; a deque per window would also work on a stream
hack2hire:69fa8ff5661bab75bbca3e10.variantLabel: Inferred single variant: throttling gateway with 3/1 s, 20/10 s, 60/60 s limits

clarifyingQuestions: Should the answer be the count of wrong sales or the list of them?
Are prices compared exactly or with a tolerance?
hints: Look up each sold product's correct price by name.
A hash map makes each lookup constant time.
Count the sales whose entered price differs from the looked-up price.
invariants: the count is between 0 and the number of sales
chooseWhen: Joining two lists on a key
tradeoffs: Exact comparison treats 2 and 2.0 as equal; a tolerance would be needed for computed prices
hack2hire:6a77ef3cd713d873ca7a9ab3.variantLabel: Inferred single variant: number of mis-priced sales

constraints: 0 <= n <= 16 (author bound for an exact search)
clarifyingQuestions: Is the answer the maximum number of days?
Can the borrower stop early, and does the last payback need covering?
How large can n be?
hints: Only the last lender of a plan and the set of used lenders matter for extending it.
For each subset, store which lenders can be last as a bitmask.
From a subset, every unused lender whose lend covers the payback of a possible last lender can be appended; the answer is the largest subset that is reachable.
invariants: reach[mask] is non-zero exactly when mask can be ordered into a valid plan
payback of the last day is never checked
chooseWhen: Small n with an order-dependent feasibility rule
tradeoffs: Exact subset search is exponential; a polynomial greedy would need a proof the author did not find
hack2hire:6a4fe73a665efda9311f575d.variantLabel: Inferred single variant: longest valid borrowing sequence

clarifyingQuestions: Are pixels connected through diagonal neighbours too?
Can two touching pixels belong to different objects?
Is the black box expensive, so calls should be minimised?
hints: Only neighbouring pixels need to be compared.
BFS from each unvisited object pixel, following neighbours the black box says are the same object.
Each BFS start is one new object; mark pixels visited when enqueued.
invariants: each object pixel is enqueued once
the black box is only called on adjacent object pixels
chooseWhen: Counting components when the equivalence is only available through a comparison oracle
tradeoffs: Comparing only neighbours is linear; comparing against one representative per object would be quadratic
hack2hire:681bafaba73bd75b806cb981.variantLabel: Inferred single variant: count objects with a black-box pixel comparison

clarifyingQuestions: Does a singer count once per role pair or once per pair of performances?
How are the rows ordered?
Are performances of the same role by the same singer paired with each other?
hints: Group performances by singer, then by role.
Two roles co-occur for a singer when their closest years are within period.
Sort each role's years and merge two sorted lists with two pointers to find the closest pair.
invariants: each (singer, role pair) contributes at most 1 in each direction
counts are symmetric: count(A, B) = count(B, A)
tradeoffs: Pairwise role checks are quadratic in roles per singer; a year sweep is better when singers have many roles but few years
hack2hire:6a21d6fcd5c5b3e5f9c345f1.variantLabel: Inferred single variant: per-singer role co-occurrence counts

clarifyingQuestions: How many frequency groups are returned, and is that a parameter?
Are words returned in lower case?
How are words within one group ordered?
hints: Lower-case the text and split on spaces, skipping empty pieces.
Count words in a hash map and collect the distinct frequencies.
The cutoff is the k-th largest distinct frequency; keep every word at or above it and sort.
invariants: every returned word has a frequency among the top k distinct frequencies
rows are sorted by (-frequency, word)
chooseWhen: Top-k by groups of equal frequency
tradeoffs: Bucket sort by frequency avoids the final sort when frequencies are small
hack2hire:69beec3021f6ab4226963c1d.variantLabel: Inferred single variant: words of the k highest frequency groups
